body.statement: If every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton, then \(M=K_0\), \(N\) has no columns, and \(b^{\star}\) is the unique feasible loading; for a single two-period panel target the resulting \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\) equals the panel-DDD efficient influence function in Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorem 5). If \(X\) is degenerate, then \(\Gamma_P(X)\) is constant and \(b^{\star}(X)=b^{\mathrm{const}}\) almost surely.
body.justification: These reductions check the operator formula against the just-identified DDD EIF and the completed constant-loading geometry.
body.gap: Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorem 5) supply the panel-DDD efficient influence function, and the constant-covariate score geometry supplies the second reduction; both must be exact special cases.
body.consumer: The reductions provide regression tests for mathematical derivations and the package backend.
